objects.description: A very simple regex-like pattern engine used by testlib to validate or generate strings. It supports character sets, quantifiers like ?, +, {m,n}, alternation with |, and grouping (). Provides matching and random generation via random_t. Instances are constructed from a pattern string and can be reused.

Pseudo-random generator used by testlib. Java-like 48-bit LCG with helpers to generate integers, reals, ranges, permutations, distinct sets, partitions, weighted distributions, and pattern-based strings. A global instance rnd is provided. Seed can be set from argv or explicit value. Version controls compatibility of bit generation.
Abstract interface for reading characters from an input source with support for unread, EOF, and line tracking. Concrete implementations wrap strings or files and are used by InStream.
Concrete InputStreamReader over an in-memory std::string. Supports unread and EOFC handling. Used by InStream(String variant) to create virtual streams from strings.
Buffered wrapper around std::FILE with undo support, tracking read characters and line numbers. Used when InStream is attached to stdio handles.
High-performance buffered reader over FILE with an internal buffer and limited unread capability. Used by InStream for non-stdio files to speed up reading.

High-level input stream used throughout testlib for reading and validating contestant/output/answer files. Wraps an InputStreamReader, provides rich reading methods with validation, error reporting, and quit handling. Three global instances exist: inf, ouf, ans.

Holds validator session metadata and analysis such as bounds hits, constant bounds, variables and features. Writes logs and markup. A single global instance 'validator' is defined and used when running in validator mode.
Helper struct tracking whether minimum and maximum bounds were hit for a variable in validator runs. EPS used for floating comparisons.
Represents a constant bound candidate for a variable across inputs; tracks whether a consistent short string value exists or the bound became inconsistent (broken).
Pair of potential constant lower/upper bounds used by Validator to log stable limits for variables.

RAII guard enforcing proper finalization rules depending on mode: checker must quit, validator must readEof, ensures opts usage, and triggers logs/markup emission. A global instance testlibFinalizeGuard exists.
Holds checker metadata (testset, group) and initialization state for accessors that require registerTestlibCmd(argc,argv). A single global instance 'checker'.
Represents a single parsed command-line opt: its raw string value and whether it was consumed by the program. Used internally by the opts subsystem.
Serializable record of a single test execution used by the scorer mode: includes verdict, points, resources, IO snapshots and checker comment.
Callable type used by registerScorer to compute total score from a vector of TestResult. Note: this is a referenced standard library type; no definition present in this header.
RAII helper that, in scorer mode, reads all TestResult lines from stdin at program end and prints the calculated score using the registered scorer function. A global instance ensures auto-run.
Referenced as latestFeatures[] global; it's an array of const char* (not a custom type). Ignored for custom types extraction.
Mode of an InStream: indicates whether the stream represents input, output, or answer. Affects behavior of quit and formatting.
Outcome codes used by testlib to report checker/validator/interactor results. Map to specific process exit codes via resultExitCode.
Global operating mode of testlib, set by various register* functions and used to adjust behavior (e.g., quit handling, input strictness).

objects.description: Verdict enumeration for a single test run used by the scorer subsystem and serialization functions.

functions.name: testlib_format_
functions.description: Formats a printf-style C string and variadic arguments into a std::string. Use in places where you need formatted strings without managing buffers.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with the provided arguments.
Caller must pass arguments matching the format specifiers to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: testlib_format_
functions.description: Formats a printf-style format held in a std::string with variadic arguments into a std::string.
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string compatible with provided arguments.
Caller must pass arguments matching the format specifiers to avoid undefined behavior.

functions.name: testlib_format_
functions.description: Formats a string using printf-style formatting into an std::string. Safe wrapper using an internal static buffer guard.
requirements: fmt must match variadic args. Not thread-safe due to shared buffer.

functions.name: setTestCase
functions.description: Sets the current test case index for validator/checker messaging and markup. In validator mode it also records the test case in the input stream to enable markup extraction.
requirements: If first call is with 0, zero-based indexing is assumed and will be adjusted internally.
In validator mode, may only be used with the global inf stream via InStream::setTestCase internally.
testCase must be in [1, 1073741823] effectively used for markup; negative not allowed.

functions.name: doubleCompare
functions.signature: inline bool doubleCompare(double expected, double result, double MAX_DOUBLE_ERROR);
functions.description: Compares two floating-point values within an absolute/relative tolerance and with special handling for NaN and infinity.
requirements: MAX_DOUBLE_ERROR should be non-negative to represent tolerance.
Handles NaN/Infinity specially; caller should be aware of semantics: NaN equals only NaN; infinities must match sign.

functions.name: doubleDelta
functions.signature: inline double doubleDelta(double expected, double result);
functions.description: Returns a combined distance metric between expected and result: min(absolute, relative) where relative is |result-expected|/|expected| when |expected|>1E-9, otherwise absolute error.

functions.name: vtos
functions.signature: template<typename T> static std::string vtos(const T &t);
functions.description: Converts a value to its string representation. For integral types it uses a fast custom conversion; otherwise it falls back to stringstream.
requirements: For integral types, supports signed and unsigned built-ins.
For non-integral types, requires operator<< to std::ostream to be defined.

functions.name: toHumanReadableString
functions.signature: template<typename T> static std::string toHumanReadableString(const T &n);
functions.description: Converts an integer to a compact human-readable string using 10^k notation when the number ends with many zeros (>=7). Signed and unsigned overloads are selected via type traits.
requirements: Intended for integer-like types; behavior for non-integral custom types is not provided.
For signed overload, negative values are supported.

functions.name: toString
functions.signature: template<typename T> static std::string toString(const T &t);
functions.description: Alias that forwards to vtos to get a string representation of t.
requirements: Requires the same as vtos for the type T.

functions.name: prepareOpts
functions.description: Parses command-line arguments into the testlib opts system. Supports -k=v, -k v, -kNN, --key forms, and stores results in __testlib_opts and __testlib_argv.
requirements: argc must be >= 0.
argv entries are expected to be null-terminated C strings.
Should be called once per process start; re-calling resets previous opts.

functions.name: prepareOpts
functions.description: Parses all command-line arguments into the global opts map and argv vector for later opt() retrieval.
requirements: argc ≥ 0; otherwise terminates with __testlib_fail.
Stores argv[0..argc-1] as strings in __testlib_argv; indexes used by opt(int).

functions.name: testlib_fopen_
functions.signature: FILE* testlib_fopen_(const char* path, const char* mode);
functions.description: Wrapper for fopen that uses fopen_s on MSVC for safer opening, otherwise std::fopen. Returns nullptr on failure.
requirements: path and mode must be valid null-terminated strings.
Caller must handle nullptr return and close the returned FILE* when done.

functions.name: testlib_freopen_
functions.signature: FILE* testlib_freopen_(const char* path, const char* mode, FILE* file);
functions.description: Wrapper for freopen that uses freopen_s on MSVC. Reopens the given stream to a new file. Returns nullptr on failure.
requirements: path and mode must be valid null-terminated strings.
file must be a valid FILE* stream.
Caller must handle nullptr return.

functions.name: pattern::next
functions.description: Generates a random string that matches the compiled regex-like testlib pattern using the provided random generator.
requirements: Generation fails (exits) if the pattern contains '*' quantifier (unbounded).
rnd must be a properly initialized random_t.
Pattern must be valid; otherwise construction would have failed earlier.

functions.name: pattern::matches
functions.description: Checks whether the entire string s matches the compiled testlib pattern.
requirements: The pattern must be a valid compiled pattern.
Matches are greedy within char-sets and support alternations.

functions.name: pattern::src
functions.description: Returns the original source string used to construct this pattern.

functions.name: random_t::setSeed
functions.description: Seeds the random generator by hashing the command-line arguments for reproducibility across runs with same argv.
requirements: argc and argv must describe valid null-terminated C strings.
Intended to be called by registerGen; it resets internal seed to a function of argv.

functions.name: random_t::setSeed
functions.description: Sets the random generator seed to a specific value (after xor with multiplier and masked to 48 bits).
requirements: No specific range constraints; any 64-bit value is accepted.

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.description: Generates a random string that matches the given pattern string by constructing a pattern and delegating to pattern::next.
requirements: ptrn must be a valid testlib pattern without '*' quantifiers for generation.
random_t must be initialized/seeded to ensure reproducibility if needed.

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.description: Borland-compatible overload: generates a random string matching the given pattern.
requirements: Same as random_t::next(const std::string&).

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.description: Returns a uniformly distributed integer in [0, n-1].
requirements: n must be positive (>0); otherwise the function fails and aborts.

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.description: Returns a uniformly distributed unsigned integer in [0, n-1].
requirements: n must be less than INT_MAX; otherwise aborts.

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.description: Returns a uniformly distributed long long in [0, n-1].
requirements: n must be positive (>0); otherwise aborts.

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.signature: unsigned long long random_t::next(unsigned long long n);
functions.description: Returns a uniformly distributed unsigned long long in [0, n-1].
requirements: n must be less than LONGLONG_MAX; otherwise aborts.

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.description: Returns a uniformly distributed long in [0, n-1].
requirements: n must be positive (>0).

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.description: Returns a uniformly distributed unsigned long in [0, n-1].
requirements: n must be less than LONG_MAX; otherwise aborts.

functions.name: random_t::next
functions.description: Returns a uniformly distributed int in [from, to].
requirements: No explicit precondition in code; implicit that the range length fits into long long arithmetic.

functions.name: random_t::next

functions.name: random_t::wnext
functions.description: Returns a weighted random int in [0, n) skewed by 'type' using repeated max/min or power transform. Positive type biases to larger values, negative to smaller.
requirements: n must be positive (>0); aborts otherwise.
Large |type| uses power transform with internal limit 'lim'.

functions.name: random_t::wnext
functions.signature: long long random_t::wnext(long long n, int type);
functions.description: Weighted random long long in [0, n) with bias 'type'.
requirements: n must be positive (>0).

functions.description: Weighted random double in [0, n) with bias 'type'.
requirements: n must be positive (>0).

functions.name: random_t::wnext

requirements: n must be less than INT_MAX; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: random_t::wnext
functions.signature: unsigned long long random_t::wnext(unsigned long long n, int type);
functions.description: Weighted random unsigned long long in [0, n).
requirements: n must be less than LONGLONG_MAX; aborts otherwise.

functions.description: Weighted random long in [0, n).

functions.description: Weighted random unsigned long in [0, n).
requirements: n must be less than LONG_MAX; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: random_t::wnext

requirements: from must be <= to; aborts otherwise.

functions.description: Weighted random int in [from, to] for unsigned inputs.
requirements: from must be <= to; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: random_t::wany
functions.signature: template<typename Container> typename Container::value_type random_t::wany(const Container &c, int type);
functions.description: Returns a weighted-random element from a container using index chosen by wnext(size, type).

Container must support size(), begin(), and be indexable via iterator advancement.

functions.name: random_t::wany

functions.description: Returns a weighted-random element from an iterator range using index chosen by wnext(size, type).
requirements: Distance between begin and end must be positive (>0).
Iterators must support std::distance and std::advance.

functions.name: random_t::perm
functions.signature: template<typename T, typename E> std::vector<E> random_t::perm(T size, E first);
functions.description: Generates a random permutation of given size with values [first, first+size-1] using internal PRNG.
requirements: size must be non-negative; aborts if negative.
If size==0 returns empty vector.

functions.name: random_t::perm
functions.description: Generates a random permutation of given size with values [0, size-1].
requirements: size must be non-negative; aborts if negative.

functions.name: random_t::distinct
functions.signature: template<typename T> std::vector<T> random_t::distinct(int size, T from, T to);
functions.description: Returns 'size' distinct numbers in [from, to] in unspecified order. Uses set sampling or permutation depending on expected effort.
requirements: from must be <= to; aborts otherwise.
size must be >= 0 and <= to-from+1; aborts otherwise.
If to-from+1 > 1e9, aborts when falling back to permutation path.

functions.name: random_t::distinct
functions.signature: template<typename T> std::vector<T> random_t::distinct(int size, T upper);
functions.description: Returns 'size' distinct numbers in [0, upper-1] in unspecified order.
requirements: size must be >= 0; aborts otherwise.
upper must be > 0; aborts otherwise.
size must be <= upper; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: random_t::partition
functions.signature: template<typename T> std::vector<T> random_t::partition(int size, T sum, T min_part);
functions.description: Produces a random composition of 'sum' into 'size' parts each >= min_part, returned unordered.
requirements: size must be >= 0; aborts otherwise.
If size==0 then sum must be 0; aborts otherwise.
min_part * size must be <= sum; aborts otherwise.
Internal sanity checks ensure sum of parts equals sum and each part >= min_part.

functions.name: random_t::partition
functions.signature: template<typename T> std::vector<T> random_t::partition(int size, T sum);
functions.description: Shortcut for partition(size, sum, 1).
requirements: Same as the 3-argument partition.

functions.name: InStream::setTestCase
functions.description: Records the testCase marker into the input stream for validator-mode to support markup extraction. Intended for inf only in validators.
requirements: May be used only for inf InStream in validator mode and when reading from std input; aborts otherwise.
testCase must fit [1, 1073741823].

functions.name: InStream::getReadChars
functions.description: Returns the sequence of raw chars read from inf (with test case markers) to support markup writing. Validator/inf only.
requirements: May be used only for inf InStream in validator mode and std input; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: resultExitCode
functions.description: Maps a testlib TResult to a process exit code respecting configured macros and partially-correct offset.

functions.name: halt
functions.description: Terminates the process with the given exit code after printing footer information if enabled. Sets __testlib_exitCode and exits (or throws if configured).
requirements: Non-returning; caller should not expect continuation.

functions.name: InStream::quit
functions.signature: NORETURN void InStream::quit(TResult result, const char *msg);
functions.description: Terminates the program with the given result and message, formatting output, writing report files, enforcing dirt checks, and closing streams.
requirements: If result indicates success/points, ensures no extra output unless interactor.
Truncates message if exceeds maxMessageLength.
In checker mode, should be used to finish with a verdict.

functions.name: InStream::quitf
functions.signature: NORETURN void InStream::quitf(TResult result, const char *msg, ...);
functions.description: printf-style variant of quit that formats the message before quitting.
requirements: Format string and arguments must match.

functions.name: InStream::quitif
functions.signature: void InStream::quitif(bool condition, TResult result, const char *msg, ...);
functions.description: Conditionally quits with formatted message if condition is true.
requirements: Format string and arguments must match when condition is true.

functions.name: InStream::quits
functions.signature: NORETURN void InStream::quits(TResult result, std::string msg);
functions.description: String variant of quit.

functions.name: InStream::xmlSafeWrite
functions.description: Writes a string to a file escaping XML-sensitive characters (&,<,>,"). Non-printable control chars (<=31) are replaced with '.'.
requirements: file must be a valid FILE* open for writing.
msg must be a valid null-terminated string.

functions.name: InStream::quitscrS
functions.description: Prints a colored message to stderr when not writing to a result file. Convenience wrapper over quitscr.

functions.name: InStream::quitscr
functions.description: Prints a colored message to stderr if not writing to a result file.
requirements: msg must be a valid C string.

functions.name: InStream::reset
functions.description: Reopens or (re-)initializes the underlying reader for the stream from a FILE* or from a named file if not standard stream. Sets binary mode on Win and constructs appropriate reader.
requirements: Cannot reset a standard handle if already opened; aborts in that case.
If non-stdfile and file is NULL, attempts to open name as file; aborts with appropriate verdict if missing depending on mode.
Caller should not use the stream concurrently.

functions.name: InStream::init
functions.description: Initializes stream to read from a file by name with mode (input/output/answer). Validates file size against maxFileSize and constructs buffered reader.
requirements: fileName must be accessible.
If file size exceeds maxFileSize, quits with _pe.
For output/answer missing files, quits with _pe/_fail respectively.

functions.name: InStream::init
functions.description: Initializes stream to read from an existing FILE* (stdin/stdout/stderr recognized as standard). Constructs appropriate reader.
requirements: f should be a valid FILE*. Sets name to standard names when applicable.

functions.name: InStream::skipBom
functions.description: Skips a UTF-8 BOM at the current position if present by peeking/consuming bytes, otherwise leaves stream unchanged.

functions.name: InStream::curChar
functions.description: Returns current character without advancing the stream (EOFC if eof).
requirements: Stream must be opened/initialized.

functions.name: InStream::nextChar
functions.description: Returns current character and advances the stream by one (EOFC if eof).

functions.name: InStream::readChar
functions.description: Reads and returns the next character (alias of nextChar).

functions.name: InStream::readChar
functions.description: Reads the next character and ensures it equals c; quits with _pe on mismatch.
requirements: Expects exact character match; treats EOLNs specially in error message.

functions.name: InStream::readSpace
functions.description: Reads and ensures the next character is a space (' ').

functions.name: InStream::unreadChar
functions.description: Pushes back a character into the stream (at most one char semantics depends on reader).
requirements: Must not underflow internal buffer; unread at pos 0 in StringInputStreamReader aborts.

functions.name: InStream::skipChar
functions.description: Skips one character (advances position by one without returning it).

functions.name: InStream::skipBlanks
functions.description: Skips blank characters (LF, CR, SPACE, TAB).

functions.name: InStream::readWord
functions.description: Reads the next non-space token (sequence of non-blank chars). In non-strict mode skips leading blanks. Errors on EOF/blank as first char.
requirements: Token length must be <= maxTokenLength; otherwise quits with _pe.

functions.name: InStream::readWord
functions.description: Reads a token and ensures it matches the given testlib pattern string; quits with _wa on mismatch. Optionally annotates variable name in validator logs.
requirements: Pattern must be valid; if strict and variableName non-empty, variable info is recorded.

functions.name: InStream::readWordTo
functions.description: Reads the next token into result with same semantics as readWord.
requirements: Resulting token length must be <= maxTokenLength; otherwise quits with _pe.

functions.name: InStream::readWordTo
functions.signature: void InStream::readWordTo(std::string &result, const pattern &p, const std::string &variableName = "");
functions.description: Reads a token into result and validates against a compiled pattern.

functions.name: InStream::readWordTo
functions.signature: void InStream::readWordTo(std::string &result, const std::string &ptrn, const std::string &variableName = "");
functions.description: Reads a token into result and validates against a pattern string.

functions.name: InStream::readToken
functions.description: Alias for readWord.

functions.name: InStream::readToken
functions.description: Reads a token and validates it against a compiled pattern.

functions.name: InStream::readTokenTo
functions.description: Alias for readWordTo.

functions.name: InStream::readTokenTo
functions.description: Reads the next space-delimited token from the stream into result. In non-strict mode leading whitespace is skipped. Fails on unexpected EOF, whitespace where a token is expected, or token length > maxTokenLength.
requirements: Stream must be opened (reader != NULL).
In non-strict mode, unexpected EOF causes _unexpected_eof (unless disabled); in strict mode it’s an error.
If the token contains embedded NULs it is transformed by __testlib_part only for messages; reading stops at whitespace/EOF.
Token length must not exceed maxTokenLength (default 32 MB).
On error the function terminates the program via quit with appropriate code.

functions.name: InStream::readTokenTo
functions.signature: void InStream::readTokenTo(std::string &result, const pattern &p, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Reads the next token into result and verifies it matches the given testlib pattern p. If variableName is provided and stream is strict (validator), validator metadata is updated. On mismatch, quits with _wa and a message identifying the variable or position.
requirements: Same reading constraints as readTokenTo(std::string&).
Pattern p must be valid (constructed earlier); generation-only constructs like '*' are rejected at pattern construction, not here.
If variableName is non-empty and stream is strict, it will be registered in validator.
On mismatch, terminates with _wa; on read errors/_unexpected_eof/_pe, terminates accordingly.

functions.name: InStream::readWords
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> InStream::readWords(int size, const pattern &p, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1);
functions.description: Reads 'size' tokens, each matching pattern p. In strict mode records variable name. Optionally expects single spaces between items when strict.
requirements: size must be non-negative and at most 1e8; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: InStream::readWords
functions.description: Reads 'size' tokens without pattern validation.
requirements: size must be non-negative and at most 1e8; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: InStream::readWords
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> InStream::readWords(int size, const std::string &ptrn, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1);
functions.description: Reads 'size' tokens, each matching the given pattern string.
requirements: size must be non-negative and at most 1e8; aborts otherwise.
Pattern must be valid.

functions.name: InStream::readTokens
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> InStream::readTokens(int size, const pattern &p, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1);
functions.description: Reads 'size' tokens and validates each against a compiled pattern p.
requirements: size must be non-negative and at most 1e8; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: InStream::readTokens
functions.description: Reads 'size' tokens without pattern validation.
requirements: size must be non-negative and at most 1e8; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: InStream::readTokens
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> InStream::readTokens(int size, const std::string &ptrn, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1);
functions.description: Reads 'size' tokens validated against a pattern string.
requirements: size must be non-negative and at most 1e8; aborts otherwise.

functions.name: InStream::readInteger
functions.description: Reads a signed 32-bit integer token and returns it. In non-strict mode skips leading whitespace. Validates format as integer and range fits into int32.
requirements: Token must be a valid decimal integer (optional leading '-'), no leading zeros except single zero; length ≤ 20.
Value must be within [INT_MIN, INT_MAX].
On EOF when value expected: quits with _unexpected_eof (non-strict) or error.
On format/range violations quits with _pe.

functions.name: InStream::readInteger
functions.signature: int InStream::readInteger(int minv, int maxv, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Alias of readInt(minv,maxv,variableName).
requirements: Same as readInt(minv,maxv,variableName).

functions.name: InStream::readLong
functions.description: Reads a signed 64-bit integer token (long long) and returns it. Performs strict format validation (no invalid chars, no leading zeros unless zero).
requirements: Token must be valid decimal integer; length 1..20, optional leading '-'.
Leading zeros are not allowed unless number is exactly 0 (and not negative).
On format violations quits with _pe; on unexpected EOF quits accordingly.

functions.name: InStream::readLong
functions.signature: long long InStream::readLong(long long minv, long long maxv, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Reads a signed 64-bit integer and ensures it lies in [minv, maxv]. In validators, may record bounds hits for variableName.
requirements: minv and maxv are caller-provided; function does not swap them.
If value ∉ [minv,maxv], quits with _wa and a human-readable bounds message.
If variableName is non-empty and stream is strict, validator bounds/constant bounds and variable are recorded.

functions.name: InStream::readLong
functions.signature: unsigned long long InStream::readLong(unsigned long long minv, unsigned long long maxv, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Alias wrapper that delegates to readUnsignedLong(minv,maxv,variableName). Provided for API symmetry.
requirements: Same as readUnsignedLong(minv,maxv,variableName).

functions.name: InStream::readUnsignedLong
functions.description: Reads an unsigned 64-bit integer token and returns it. Performs strict format validation and rejects leading zeros for multi-digit values.
requirements: Token must be digits only, length 1..20.
If length > 1 the first digit must not be '0'.
On format violations quits with _pe; on unexpected EOF quits accordingly.

functions.name: InStream::readUnsignedLong
functions.signature: unsigned long long InStream::readUnsignedLong(unsigned long long minv, unsigned long long maxv, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Reads an unsigned 64-bit integer and ensures it lies in [minv,maxv]. In validators, may record bounds hits for variableName.
requirements: minv and maxv are caller-provided.
If value ∉ [minv,maxv], quits with _wa and index/variable-aware message.
If variableName is non-empty and strict, validator bounds/constant bounds and variable are recorded.

functions.signature: std::vector<long long> InStream::readLongs(int size, int indexBase = 1)

In strict mode, requires a single space between elements (except last).
On read/format errors, quits with appropriate code.

functions.name: InStream::readUnsignedLongs
functions.signature: std::vector<unsigned long long> InStream::readUnsignedLongs(int size, int indexBase = 1)
functions.description: Reads size space-separated unsigned 64-bit values without additional range checks. Returns as vector<unsigned long long>.
requirements: size must be non-negative and ≤ 100000000.
In strict mode, requires a single space between elements (except last).

functions.name: InStream::readInt
functions.signature: int InStream::readInt(int minv, int maxv, const std::string &variableName = "")

requirements: minv and maxv are caller-provided; no reordering.

If variableName non-empty and strict, validator metadata is updated.

functions.name: InStream::readInts
functions.description: Reads size space-separated int values without range checks.
requirements: size must be non-negative and ≤ 100000000.
In strict mode, expects a single space between items (except last).

functions.signature: std::vector<int> InStream::readIntegers(int size, int minv, int maxv, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1)

requirements: Same as readInts(size,minv,maxv,variablesName,indexBase).

functions.description: Reads size ints without range checks. Synonym for readInts(size,indexBase).
requirements: Same as readInts(size,indexBase).

functions.name: InStream::readReal
functions.description: Reads a floating-point token as double with permissive format (digits, optional '.', 'e'/'E', sign). Validates it parses and is not NaN.
requirements: Token may contain digits, '.', 'e'/'E', '+'/'-'.
At least one digit required; at most one decimal point and exponent char; minus/plus counts ≤ 2; exponent count ≤ 1.
Parses via sscanf; NaN is rejected; on invalid, quits with _pe.
In non-strict mode, unexpected EOF yields _unexpected_eof.

functions.name: InStream::readReal
functions.signature: double InStream::readReal(double minv, double maxv, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Reads a double and ensures it lies in [minv,maxv]. For strict streams and named variables, updates validator bounds hits/constant bounds.
requirements: minv and maxv provided by caller.
If result ∉ [minv,maxv], quits with _wa; index-aware messages when used in batch readers.
If variableName non-empty and strict, records hit when result is within EPS of bounds.

functions.name: InStream::readDouble
functions.description: Alias of readReal().
requirements: Same as readReal().

functions.name: InStream::readDouble
functions.signature: double InStream::readDouble(double minv, double maxv, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Alias of readReal(minv,maxv,variableName).
requirements: Same as readReal(minv,maxv,variableName).

functions.description: Reads size doubles each in [minv,maxv]. Returns vector<double>.
requirements: size must be non-negative and ≤ 100000000.
Each element must be within [minv,maxv] else _wa; index reported from indexBase.
In strict mode, a single space between elements is required.

functions.name: InStream::readReals
functions.description: Reads size doubles without range checks. Returns vector<double>.
requirements: size must be non-negative and ≤ 100000000.
In strict mode, requires a single space between items (except last).

functions.name: InStream::readDoubles
functions.signature: std::vector<double> InStream::readDoubles(int size, double minv, double maxv, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1)
functions.description: Reads size doubles each constrained to [minv,maxv]. Returns vector<double>.
requirements: Same constraints as readReals(size,minv,maxv,...).

functions.name: InStream::readDoubles
functions.description: Reads size doubles without range checks. Returns vector<double>.
requirements: Same as readReals(size,indexBase).

functions.name: InStream::readStrictReal
functions.signature: double InStream::readStrictReal(double minv, double maxv, int minAfterPointDigitCount, int maxAfterPointDigitCount, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Reads a strictly formatted decimal real number and enforces both numeric bounds and digit count after the decimal point. Format: optional '-', then digits, optional single '.', then digits; no exponent, no leading zeros in integer part unless the number is 0. Not NaN/Inf.
requirements: minAfterPointDigitCount ≥ 0 and ≤ maxAfterPointDigitCount; otherwise _fail.
Token length 1..1000; first char is '-' or digit; last char must be digit.
At most one '.'; all other chars must be digits.
Digits after '.' must be within [minAfterPointDigitCount, maxAfterPointDigitCount].
No exponent allowed; no invalid characters.
If numeric value ∉ [minv,maxv], quits with _wa; otherwise returns the parsed double.
If variableName non-empty and strict, validator bounds/variables updated.

functions.name: InStream::readStrictReals
functions.signature: std::vector<double> InStream::readStrictReals(int size, double minv, double maxv, int minAfterPointDigitCount, int maxAfterPointDigitCount, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1)
functions.description: Reads size strictly formatted reals with digit-count and range constraints. Returns vector<double>.
requirements: size must be non-negative and ≤ 100000000.
All per-element constraints are those of readStrictReal(...).
In strict mode, requires a single space between elements (except last).

functions.name: InStream::readStrictDouble
functions.signature: double InStream::readStrictDouble(double minv, double maxv, int minAfterPointDigitCount, int maxAfterPointDigitCount, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Alias of readStrictReal(minv,maxv,minAfterPointDigitCount,maxAfterPointDigitCount,variableName).
requirements: Same as readStrictReal(...)

functions.name: InStream::readStrictDoubles
functions.signature: std::vector<double> InStream::readStrictDoubles(int size, double minv, double maxv, int minAfterPointDigitCount, int maxAfterPointDigitCount, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1)
functions.description: Reads size strictly formatted doubles each constrained by value and fractional digit count. Returns vector<double>.
requirements: Same constraints as readStrictReals(size,...).

functions.name: InStream::eof
functions.description: Returns true if the underlying reader is at EOF. In non-strict mode, returns true if reader is NULL.
requirements: None beyond stream existence; safe if reader is NULL (non-strict returns true).

functions.name: InStream::seekEof
functions.description: Skips blanks (whitespace) and then checks eof(). In non-strict mode returns true if reader is NULL.
requirements: None; uses skipBlanks() which consumes whitespace.

functions.name: InStream::eoln
functions.description: Checks whether the current position is at end-of-line without consuming it; updates internal position carefully. In strict mode, only accepts CRLF on Windows or LF on others as EOLN as per compile-time conditions.
requirements: On non-strict, EOLN is true for LF, CRLF, or EOFC; otherwise false and unreadChar restores state.
On strict Windows builds expects CR followed by LF; on others expects LF. If mismatch, restores state and returns false.

functions.name: InStream::readEoln
functions.description: Requires EOLN at current position and consumes it. Quits with _pe on failure.
requirements: Relies on eoln(); if false, quits with _pe "Expected EOLN".
Updates lastLine before check.

functions.name: InStream::readEof
functions.description: Requires EOF at current position. Quits with _pe on failure. In validators, increments finalize guard counter on inf.
requirements: If not EOF, quits with _pe "Expected EOF".
If called on inf and finalize guard alive, marks readEofCount for finalization checks.

functions.name: InStream::seekEoln
functions.description: Skips spaces and tabs, then checks eoln() without consuming non-EOL characters (restores one char).
requirements: None specific; uses nextChar()/unreadChar to restore state before calling eoln().

functions.name: InStream::nextLine
functions.description: Moves to the next line by reading and discarding the current line (delegates to readLine()).
requirements: Underlying stream must be open. Errors in readStringTo/readEoln cause termination.

functions.name: InStream::readStringTo
functions.description: Reads the rest of the current line into result without the line terminator. In strict mode, enforces and consumes EOLN; in non-strict, attempts to consume EOLN but not enforced.
requirements: If reader is NULL, quits with _pe "Expected line".
Stops before LF or CRLF; handles CR followed by LF as a Windows line ending.
In strict mode, requires EOLN (via readEoln()), otherwise just calls eoln() to advance appropriately.

functions.name: InStream::readStringTo
functions.signature: void InStream::readStringTo(std::string &result, const pattern &p, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Reads a line into result and checks it matches pattern p. On mismatch quits with _wa, mentioning variableName if provided; in strict mode records variable.
requirements: Same line-reading constraints as readStringTo.
Pattern must match the entire line (no trailing content).

functions.name: InStream::readStringTo
functions.signature: void InStream::readStringTo(std::string &result, const std::string &ptrn, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Reads a line into result, checks it against pattern string ptrn (compiled to pattern).
requirements: ptrn must be a valid testlib pattern.
Other constraints as above.

functions.name: InStream::readString
functions.description: Convenience returning version of readStringTo: reads the current line (without terminator) and returns it.
requirements: Same as readStringTo(std::string&).

functions.name: InStream::readString
functions.description: Reads a line and ensures it matches pattern p; returns the line. Variable tracking as in other pattern-checked readers.
requirements: Same as readStringTo(result,p,variableName).

functions.name: InStream::readString
functions.description: Reads a line and ensures it matches pattern ptrn; returns the line.
requirements: ptrn must be valid testlib pattern; other constraints as above.

functions.name: InStream::readStrings
functions.description: Reads size lines (without line terminators) and returns them as vector<string>.
requirements: size must be non-negative and ≤ 100000000.
In strict mode, demands proper EOLN per line.

functions.name: InStream::readStrings
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> InStream::readStrings(int size, const pattern &p, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1)
functions.description: Reads size lines, each of which must match pattern p. Returns vector<string>.
requirements: size must be non-negative and ≤ 100000000.
On mismatch for any element, quits with _wa and reports its index (starting at indexBase).
In strict mode, records variablesName if provided.

functions.name: InStream::readStrings
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> InStream::readStrings(int size, const std::string &ptrn, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1)
functions.description: Reads size lines, each of which must match pattern ptrn. Returns vector<string>.
requirements: Same constraints as readStrings(size, pattern, ...).

functions.name: InStream::readLineTo
functions.description: Alias of readStringTo(result). Reads current line into result (without terminator).
requirements: Same as readStringTo(result).

functions.name: InStream::readLineTo
functions.signature: void InStream::readLineTo(std::string &result, const pattern &p, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Alias to readStringTo(result,p,variableName). Reads a line and validates pattern.
requirements: Same as readStringTo(result,p,variableName).

functions.name: InStream::readLineTo
functions.signature: void InStream::readLineTo(std::string &result, const std::string &ptrn, const std::string &variableName = "")
functions.description: Alias to readStringTo(result,ptrn,variableName).
requirements: Same as readStringTo(result,ptrn,variableName).

functions.name: InStream::readLine
functions.description: Alias of readString(). Reads and returns the current line (without terminator).
requirements: Same as readString().

functions.name: InStream::readLine
functions.description: Alias to readString(p,variableName). Returns the validated line.
requirements: Same as readString(p,variableName).

functions.name: InStream::readLine
functions.description: Alias to readString(ptrn,variableName). Returns the validated line.
requirements: Same as readString(ptrn,variableName).

functions.name: InStream::readLines
functions.description: Alias of readStrings(size,indexBase). Reads size lines and returns them.
requirements: Same as readStrings(size,indexBase).

functions.name: InStream::readLines
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> InStream::readLines(int size, const pattern &p, const std::string &variablesName = "", int indexBase = 1)

requirements: Same as readStrings(size,p,variablesName,indexBase).

requirements: Same as readStrings(size,ptrn,variablesName,indexBase).

functions.name: InStream::ensuref
functions.description: If cond is false, formats the message and quits via this->__testlib_ensure (which calls quit(_wa,...)). Used for stream-specific assertions that produce WA on output streams and FAIL on others as per quit behavior.

On cond==false, program terminates.

functions.name: InStream::__testlib_ensure
functions.description: Internal helper: if cond is false, calls this->quit(_wa,message.c_str()).
requirements: message should be non-empty for meaningful diagnostics.

functions.name: InStream::close
functions.description: Closes the underlying reader, deleting it and marking the stream as not opened.
requirements: Safe to call multiple times; after close, reader becomes NULL and opened=false.

functions.name: quit
functions.signature: NORETURN void quit(TResult result, const char *msg)
functions.description: Global quit helper: delegates to ouf.quit(result, msg).
requirements: Same as quit(TResult,const std::string&).

Always terminates.

functions.signature: NORETURN void quitp(double points, const std::string &message = "")

requirements: Same constraints as float overload.

functions.description: Terminates with computed points (long double). See float overload for constraints.
requirements: Same constraints as float overload.

functions.name: quitp
functions.signature: NORETURN void quitp(int points, const std::string &message = "")
functions.description: Terminates with computed points (int). See float overload for constraints.
requirements: Same constraints as float overload.

functions.signature:
template<typename F>

Format string must match arguments.

Always terminates.

functions.name: quitf
functions.signature: NORETURN void quitf(TResult result, const char *format, ...)

requirements: format must match arguments.

functions.name: setAppesModeEncoding
functions.description: Sets the XML encoding used in APPES mode reports. Validates the encoding against a built-in allowlist; on invalid input, terminates with _fail.
requirements: appesModeEncoding is case-insensitive; must be one of the predefined encodings list (e.g., 'windows-1251', 'utf-8', etc.).

functions.name: registerInteraction
functions.description: Initializes testlib in interactor mode. Parses command line, sets up input stream (inf), output file stream (tout), and answer stream (ans), configures result file and APPES mode if provided.
requirements: Program arguments: <input-file> <output-file> [<answer-file> [<report-file> [<-appes>]]]. On EJUDGE, different limits apply.
If --help is first arg, prints help and exits with FAIL code.
Files must be accessible; errors terminate with _fail.
Binary mode enforced for stdio on supported platforms.

functions.name: registerValidation
functions.description: Initializes testlib in validator mode, wiring inf to stdin and enabling strict mode. Also sets binary mode for stdio.
requirements: Must be called before reading input in validators.
Will be checked by finalize guard; missing readEof() will cause failure at finalize if not suppressed.

functions.name: registerValidation
functions.description: Extended validator initialization supporting command-line options for testset/group/test overview log/markup/test case extraction.

Invalid/missing values cause _fail with guidance.
Also records testset/group globally for getTestset/getGroup.

functions.name: addFeature
functions.description: Registers a feature name for validator instrumentation (to later mark as used via feature()).

functions.name: feature
functions.description: Marks a previously registered feature as used/hit for the current test in validator mode.
requirements: Must be in validator mode; otherwise _fail.
Feature name must be analyzable (no control characters).

functions.name: registerTestlibCmd
functions.description: Initializes testlib in checker mode parsing command line (with optional --testset and --group), opens inf/ouf/ans streams, and configures result output (including APPES).
requirements: Program arguments: [--testset testset] [--group group] <input-file> <output-file> <answer-file> [<report-file> [<-appes>]].
If '--help' specified, prints help and exits.
Files must be accessible; errors terminate with _fail.
Sets ouf to stdin (program output), skips BOM on ouf.

functions.name: registerTestlib
functions.description: Varargs helper that forwards to registerTestlibCmd by building a fake argv array. For legacy usage.
requirements: argc must be 3..5 corresponding to required/optional files and flags.
Arguments must be char* pointers; misuse is UB.
On invalid arg count, quits with _fail.

functions.description: Global ensure helper (not stream-bound). If cond is false, formats message and calls __testlib_ensure which quits with _fail.
requirements: format must be a printf-style string matching variadic args.
On cond == false, terminates with _fail.

functions.name: setName
functions.description: Sets the checker name for diagnostics, formatting with printf-style arguments.
requirements: format must match variadic args.

functions.name: shuffle
functions.description: Stable random shuffle using testlib's rnd (Fisher-Yates style). Use instead of std::random_shuffle. Produces deterministic results across platforms given the same rnd state.

rnd must be properly seeded for reproducibility.

functions.name: srand
functions.description: Disabled replacement for C srand(): calling it terminates with an error prompting to use registerGen(argc, argv, 1) to seed rnd.
requirements: Do not call. Always terminates with _fail.

functions.name: startTest
functions.description: In generators, redirects stdout to a file named by the given test index (as decimal string).
requirements: Opening/redirecting stdout must succeed; on failure terminates with _fail.
test is converted to string to form filename.

functions.description: Returns a sanitized/shortened representation of s by replacing embedded NULs with '~' and truncating to a compact preview for diagnostic messages.
requirements: Input can contain NULs; function maps them to '~' in output.

functions.name: englishEnding
functions.description: Returns English ordinal suffix for integer x: th/st/nd/rd with standard rules.
requirements: None.

requirements: Same as range join with separator.

functions.name: join

functions.name: tokenize
functions.description: Splits s at any of separators characters, omitting empty items.
requirements: If separators is empty, returns vector with single element s (even if empty).

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for C strings (null-terminated when used as C API). We return bytes without embedded NULs,
# since the fuzzer framework will place them into buffers/files. We keep them ASCII-printable with
# occasional extended bytes but never include \x00. Limit size to <= 4096.

PRINTABLE = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
)

# Additional interesting substrings to exercise formatting and message printing paths
INTERESTING_SUBSTRINGS = [
    "",  # empty
    "hello",
    "%s",
    "%d",
    "%llu",
    "%%",           # literal percent
    "int=%d ull=%llu s=%s",  # matches the tested format
    "a=%d b=%d",
    "line1\nline2",
    "tabs\tand\tspaces",
    "unicode-ish: \u263A",   # just backslash-u text, stays ASCII
    "<xml>&\"'<>",
]

# Some extended non-ASCII bytes excluding NUL
EXT_BYTES = [bytes([b]) for b in range(1, 256) if b not in (0,)]


def _rand_printable(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Mostly printable ASCII, occasionally insert extended bytes escaped via latin-1 decode
    s_chars: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(length):
        if rng.random() < 0.12:
            b = rng.choice(EXT_BYTES)
            s_chars.append(b.decode('latin-1'))
        else:
            s_chars.append(rng.choice(PRINTABLE))
    return "".join(s_chars)


def _mix_substrings(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a composite string from interesting substrings and random filler
    parts: List[str] = []
    count = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(count):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.45:
            parts.append(rng.choice(INTERESTING_SUBSTRINGS))
        elif choice < 0.9:
            parts.append(_rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(1, 32)))
        else:
            # biased insertion of percent signs to stress formatting consumers (but used as data)
            parts.append('%' * rng.randint(1, 5))
    s = "".join(parts)
    # Trim to a reasonable length later by the caller
    return s


def _sanitize_no_nul(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no NULs present; encode as latin-1 to preserve byte values 1..255.
    # Replace any accidental \x00 with 'X' (shouldn't occur with our construction).
    b = s.encode('latin-1', errors='replace')
    if b"\x00" in b:
        b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"X")
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a strategy: single focused string or composite
    strategy = rng.random()

    if strategy < 0.25:
        # Exact format strings that the fuzzer stub uses, to exercise happy path
        s = rng.choice([
            "int=%d ull=%llu s=%s",
            "a=%d b=%d",
        ])
    elif strategy < 0.5:
        # Short message suitable for quitscr
        base = rng.choice([
            "", "ok", "warning: something happened", "error: details follow",
            "[INFO] Start", "[DEBUG] x=42", "EOL test -> ",
        ])
        tail = _rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
        s = base + tail
    elif strategy < 0.75:
        # Composite with interesting substrings
        s = _mix_substrings(rng)
    else:
        # Random printable blob
        s = _rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(1, 256))

    # Occasionally inject newlines to test message functions; avoid leading NULs
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        nl_join = rng.choice(["\n", "\r\n", "\n\n"])
        left = _rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(0, 40))
        right = _rand_printable(rng, rng.randint(0, 40))
        s = left + nl_join + s + nl_join + right

    # Ensure size cap and remove NULs, then return bytes
    max_len = 1024  # well below 4096 cap
    if len(s) > max_len:
        s = s[:max_len]

    return _sanitize_no_nul(s)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces bytes that represent a valid filesystem path for the fuzzer's FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME().
# The fuzzer stubs expect to open/read/write files at that path, so we should provide paths that are:
# - Valid and simple (no directories) to avoid missing directories
# - Short and within typical filesystem limits
# - With a mix of extensions and characters to exercise different code paths
# The harness will create/populate files at these paths as needed; we just need a plausible filename.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_@#%+="
EXTENSIONS = [
    "", "txt", "bin", "dat", "log", "tmp", "csv", "json", "xml", "cfg",
    "in", "out", "ans", "bmp", "raw"
]
PREFIXES = [
    "test", "case", "input", "data", "longname", "a", "Z", "file", "sample", "tmp"
]

def _weighted_choice(r: random.Random, items: List[str], weights: List[int]) -> str:
    total = sum(weights)
    x = r.randrange(total)
    acc = 0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if x < acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]

def _rand_base(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a base name length between 1 and 48
    length = r.randint(1, 48)
    # Sometimes start from a prefix
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base = r.choice(PREFIXES)
    else:
        base = ""
    # Fill with safe characters
    while len(base) < length:
        base += r.choice(SAFE_CHARS)
    # Occasionally insert a few dots or dashes in the middle (but not leading/trailing)
    if r.random() < 0.3 and len(base) > 4:
        pos = r.randint(1, len(base) - 2)
        base = base[:pos] + r.choice(["-", "_", "."]) + base[pos:]
    # Trim to requested length
    return base[:length]

def _rand_ext(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        return r.choice(EXTENSIONS)
    # Sometimes random 1-4 letter extension
    return ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)))

def _rand_suffix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Add a numeric or small token suffix sometimes
    choices = ["", "-v", "_v", "-part", "_part", "-chunk", "_chunk"]
    suf = r.choice(choices)
    if suf and r.random() < 0.7:
        suf += str(r.randint(0, 9999))
    return suf

def _maybe_windows_style(r: random.Random) -> bool:
    # Avoid directories to ensure existence; rarely we can use .\\ prefix which points to cwd
    return r.random() < 0.1

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide path style (mostly relative filenames). Avoid directories that may not exist.
    prefix = ''
    if _maybe_windows_style(r):
        # Use .\\ or .// as a harmless prefix
        prefix = _weighted_choice(r, [".\\", "./"], [1, 1])

    base = _rand_base(r)
    suf = _rand_suffix(r)
    ext = _rand_ext(r)

    name = base + suf
    # Ensure no trailing dot before adding extension
    name = name.rstrip('.') or "file"

    if ext:
        filename = f"{name}.{ext}"
    else:
        filename = name

    # Ensure filename not too long and not reserved names on Windows
    reserved = {"CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL", *(f"COM{i}" for i in range(1,10)), *(f"LPT{i}" for i in range(1,10))}
    stem = filename.split('.')[0].upper()
    if stem in reserved:
        filename = "_" + filename

    path = prefix + filename

    # Bound size to 4096 bytes max
    path = path[:256]

    return path.encode('utf-8')

        first = str(r.randint(1, 9))
        rest_len = r.randint(0, 5)
        rest = ''.join(str(r.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(rest_len))
        int_part = first + rest
        neg = r.random() < 0.5
    s = ('-' if neg else '') + int_part
    if k > 0:
        frac = ''.join(str(r.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(k))
        s += '.' + frac
    return s


def _permissive_real(r: random.Random) -> str:
    int_part = str(r.randint(0, 100000))
    frac_len = r.randint(1, 6)
    frac = ''.join(str(r.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(frac_len))
    neg = r.random() < 0.5
    return ('-' if neg else '') + int_part + '.' + frac


def _xml_heavy(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    specials = ['&', '<', '>', '"']
    base = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '     ') for _ in range(max(0, n - 4)))
    extra = ''.join(r.choice(specials) for _ in range(4))
    ctrl = ''.join(chr(r.randint(1, 31)) for _ in range(r.randint(0, 3)))
    return base + extra + ctrl


def _sep_rich(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    seps = ',;|:/\\\t '
    alph = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    return ''.join(r.choice(alph + seps) for _ in range(n))


def _patternish(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    atoms = [
        _rand_token_no_space(r, 1, 5),
        '[a-z]','[0-9]','(ab|cd)','?','+','{1,3}','|','(.)'
    ]
    m = r.randint(3, 8)
    for _ in range(m):
        parts.append(r.choice(atoms))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    return s[:64]


def _filenames(r: random.Random, count: int) -> List[str]:
    exts = ['.txt', '.dat', '.bin', '.log']
    names = []
    for _ in range(count):
        stem = _rand_alnum(r, 3, 10)
        names.append(stem + r.choice(exts))
    return names


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    sections: List[str] = []

    # Clean tokens line
    n_tokens = r.randint(2, 8)
    tokens = [_rand_token_no_space(r, 1, 16) for _ in range(n_tokens)]
    sections.append('TOKENS ' + ' '.join(tokens))

    # Integer literals
    ints = [_rand_int32(r) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 8))]
    sections.append('INTS ' + ' '.join(str(v) for v in ints))

    # Signed 64-bit values
    i64s = [_rand_i64(r) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6))]
    sections.append('I64 ' + ' '.join(str(v) for v in i64s))

    # Unsigned 64-bit values
    u64s = [_rand_u64(r) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6))]
    sections.append('U64 ' + ' '.join(_unsigned_dec(v) for v in u64s))

    # Permissive reals
    reals = [_permissive_real(r) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6))]
    sections.append('REAL ' + ' '.join(reals))

    # Strict reals with constraints
    min_after = r.randint(0, 2)
    max_after = min_after + r.randint(0, 4)
    stricts = [_strict_real(r, min_after, max_after) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6))]
    sections.append(f'STRICT[{min_after},{max_after}] ' + ' '.join(stricts))

    # Several single lines
    line_count = r.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(line_count):
        line = _rand_token_no_space(r, 1, 64)
        sections.append('LINE ' + line)

    # XML-heavy snippet
    sections.append('XML ' + _xml_heavy(r, 60))

    # Separator-rich content
    sections.append('SEPS ' + _sep_rich(r, 80))

    # Format-friendly string
    fmt_plain = _rand_token_no_space(r, 5, 20)
    sections.append('FMT ' + fmt_plain)

    # Patternish candidates
    patt_count = r.randint(2, 5)
    for _ in range(patt_count):
        sections.append('PAT ' + _patternish(r))

    # Filenames
    files = _filenames(r, r.randint(2, 5))
    sections.append('FILES ' + ' '.join(files))

    blob = '\n'.join(sections) + '\n'
    data = blob.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
        while data and (data[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
            data = data[:-1]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, choices: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(choices)

# Generate a single non-blank token followed by a newline.
# The fuzzer wrappers will write our bytes verbatim to a file and then may append a newline,
# but they already ensure a trailing newline; we therefore generate only the token here.
# Still, returning bytes is required by the harness; it will be used for FUZZ_PARAM_STR or file content.
# Our goal: produce interesting yet valid tokens that cover diverse cases while avoiding any whitespace.

def _make_token(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Interesting token families: boundaries, punctuation-heavy, mixed case, unicode-ish (ASCII only here),
    # numeric-like without leading zeros, hex-like, separators avoided, long near limit, short, brackets, etc.
    families = []

    # 1) Short alphanumerics
    families.append(lambda: _alnum(rng, rng.randint(1, 8)))

    # 2) Mixed punctuation but excluding whitespace
    families.append(lambda: _from_charset(rng, string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:+#@!$%^&*()[]{}<>=?~|\\", rng.randint(3, 20)))

    # 3) Numeric-like without leading zeros (allow single zero)
    families.append(lambda: _numeric_like(rng))

    # 4) Hex-ish prefixes
    families.append(lambda: _prefix_body(rng, prefix=_rand_choice(rng, ["0x", "0X", "#", "0h"]), body_chars=string.hexdigits.replace(" ", ""), min_len=1, max_len=16))

    # 5) Path-ish tokens (no spaces)
    families.append(lambda: _pathish(rng))

    # 6) Repetition/edge lengths close to fuzzer cap (<=64 per stub); vary 60..64
    families.append(lambda: _from_charset(rng, string.ascii_lowercase, rng.randint(60, 64)))

    # 7) CamelCase with digits
    families.append(lambda: _camel_with_digits(rng, rng.randint(5, 20)))

    # 8) Email-like without spaces
    families.append(lambda: _email_like(rng))

    # 9) JSON-like single token (still whitespace-free)
    families.append(lambda: _jsonish(rng))

    token = _rand_choice(rng, families)()
    # Ensure no whitespace and non-empty
    if not token:
        token = "tok"
    token = ''.join(ch if ch not in " \t\n\r\v\f" else 'A' for ch in token)
    # Cap to 64 as the stubs truncate
    if len(token) > 64:
        token = token[:64]
    return token


def _alnum(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))


def _from_charset(rng: random.Random, charset: str, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(charset) for _ in range(n))


def _numeric_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        return "0"
    # Optional sign
    sign = rng.choice(['', '-'])
    # Generate integer without leading zeros
    first = rng.choice('123456789')
    rest_len = rng.randint(0, 18)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rest_len))
    tok = sign + first + rest
    # Occasionally add suffixes
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        tok += rng.choice(['u', 'U', 'l', 'L', 'ul', 'LL'])
    return tok


def _prefix_body(rng: random.Random, prefix: str, body_chars: str, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    body = ''.join(rng.choice(body_chars) for _ in range(length))
    return prefix + body


def _pathish(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Components without spaces, include dots and dashes
    comp_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-+"
    depth = rng.randint(1, 5)
    comps = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        clen = rng.randint(1, 10)
        comps.append(''.join(rng.choice(comp_chars) for _ in range(clen)))
    sep = rng.choice(['/','\\'])
    lead = '' if rng.random() < 0.5 else sep
    tail = '' if rng.random() < 0.7 else sep  # sometimes trailing separator
    return lead + sep.join(comps) + tail


def _camel_with_digits(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    parts = []
    while len(''.join(parts)) < n:
        head = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
        tail_len = rng.randint(0, 3)
        tail = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(tail_len))
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            tail += ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)))
        parts.append(head + tail)
    tok = ''.join(parts)
    return tok[:n]


def _email_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    local_chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._+-"  
    domain_chars = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-"
    tld_choices = ["com","net","org","io","dev","local","xyz"]
    local = ''.join(rng.choice(local_chars) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 16)))
    labels = [''.join(rng.choice(domain_chars) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10))) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
    domain = '.'.join(labels + [rng.choice(tld_choices)])
    return f"{local}@{domain}"


def _jsonish(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a compact JSON-like single-token without spaces
    # Examples: {"k":123}, [1,2,3], {"a":[true,false,null]}, but we must remove spaces.
    def lit() -> str:
        return rng.choice(["true","false","null", _numeric_like(rng)])
    def key() -> str:
        # JSON keys quoted; avoid quotes issues by using letters only
        k = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)))
        return '"' + k + '"'
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # array
        n = rng.randint(0, 5)
        items = ','.join(lit() for _ in range(n))
        return '[' + items + ']'
    else:
        # object
        n = rng.randint(0, 4)
        pairs = []
        for _ in range(n):
            pairs.append(key() + ':' + lit())
        return '{' + ','.join(pairs) + '}'


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    token = _make_token(rng)
    # Return bytes that the harness will use as initial interesting FUZZ_PARAM_STR, and
    # when written to file it will append a newline itself. Keep under 4096 bytes.
    data = token.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
